{"predictors": [
{"name": "R&D Expense Growth Volatility", "construction": "standard deviation of year-over-year changes in R&D expenses over the past 5 years, using Compustat data", "rationale": "Firms with volatile R&D expense growth may be more likely to experience future breakthroughs or setbacks, leading to higher expected returns to compensate for the increased uncertainty. This volatility can be a proxy for the firm's ability to innovate and adapt to changing market conditions.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Customer Concentration Index", "construction": "Herfindahl index of customer sales concentrations, calculated using Compustat data on sales to individual customers over the past 3 years", "rationale": "Firms with a high customer concentration index may be more vulnerable to customer-specific risks, leading to higher expected returns to compensate for this increased risk. This index can be a proxy for the firm's dependence on a few large customers.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Inventory Turnover Acceleration", "construction": "year-over-year change in inventory turnover, calculated using Compustat data on cost of goods sold and inventory levels over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with accelerating inventory turnover may be experiencing improving operational efficiency or increasing demand, leading to higher expected returns. This acceleration can be a proxy for the firm's ability to manage its supply chain and respond to changing market conditions.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Capital Expenditure Reversal", "construction": "year-over-year change in capital expenditures, calculated using Compustat data over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms that reverse a prior trend of increasing capital expenditures may be signaling a shift in their investment strategy or a response to changing market conditions, leading to higher expected returns. This reversal can be a proxy for the firm's ability to adapt to changing market conditions.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Accounts Payable Days Growth", "construction": "year-over-year change in accounts payable days, calculated using Compustat data on accounts payable and cost of goods sold over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with growing accounts payable days may be experiencing improving supplier relationships or increasing bargaining power, leading to higher expected returns. This growth can be a proxy for the firm's ability to manage its supply chain and negotiate with suppliers.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Employee Growth Rate Dispersion", "construction": "standard deviation of year-over-year changes in employee count over the past 5 years, using Compustat data", "rationale": "Firms with high dispersion in employee growth rates may be experiencing changing business conditions or shifting investment strategies, leading to higher expected returns to compensate for the increased uncertainty. This dispersion can be a proxy for the firm's ability to adapt to changing market conditions.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Trade Receivable Days Deceleration", "construction": "year-over-year change in trade receivable days, calculated using Compustat data on trade receivables and sales over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with decelerating trade receivable days may be experiencing improving customer relationships or increasing bargaining power, leading to higher expected returns. This deceleration can be a proxy for the firm's ability to manage its customer base and negotiate with customers.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "PP&E Obsolescence Risk", "construction": "ratio of net PP&E to gross PP&E, calculated using Compustat data over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with high PP&E obsolescence risk may be more vulnerable to technological disruption or changing market conditions, leading to higher expected returns to compensate for this increased risk. This risk can be a proxy for the firm's dependence on outdated technology or assets.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "SG&A Expense Ratio Volatility", "construction": "standard deviation of year-over-year changes in SG&A expense ratio over the past 5 years, using Compustat data", "rationale": "Firms with volatile SG&A expense ratios may be experiencing changing business conditions or shifting investment strategies, leading to higher expected returns to compensate for the increased uncertainty. This volatility can be a proxy for the firm's ability to manage its operating expenses and adapt to changing market conditions.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Intangible Asset Growth", "construction": "year-over-year change in intangible assets, calculated using Compustat data over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with growing intangible assets may be investing in research and development, brands, or other intangible assets that can drive future growth and innovation, leading to higher expected returns. This growth can be a proxy for the firm's ability to invest in its future growth and competitiveness.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}
]}
